::: {.csf-hero}
<p class="csf-hero__eyebrow">Since March 2022</p>

<h1 class="csf-hero__title">It started because nobody knew their <em>neighbours</em></h1>

<p class="csf-hero__lede">
Cuochi senza fuochi began in March 2022 as a dinner between people who lived in the
same few streets in Padova and had never spoken to each other.
</p>
:::

::: {.csf-section}
<h2 class="csf-section__title">The problem we noticed</h2>

Arriving in a new city follows a script. You find a room you can afford. You work
out how to get to the university or the office. Both of those get solved in the
first month, because both of them have a market, a price and a contract.

Then the script runs out. There is no listing site for *people who live near you and
would also like someone to eat with*. Full-time work or a full course load leaves
almost no room to go looking, and the standard options are worse than they sound:
bars charge you every time, clubs are too loud to talk in, and apps hand you back
the same screen you were trying to get away from.

So the format was deliberately kept as simple as possible: **one table, one dish each,
somebody's flat, no money changing hands.**

::: {.csf-quote}
With a room and a commute, the capital is guaranteed. But what about human capital?
Is it easy to find new like-minded people? Working full-time makes it too hard.

<cite>— the note that started the whole thing, March 2022</cite>
:::
:::

::: {.csf-section}
<h2 class="csf-section__title">Why "cooks without fires"</h2>

Because none of us had a real kitchen. Student rooms and shared flats come with two
hobs that half work, no oven, and a fridge shared between five people. That could
have been the reason not to do it. Instead it became the constraint that defined it:
if the dish needs no fire, everyone can take part, including the person who has
never cooked anything in their life.

It also keeps the door genuinely open. The barrier to entry is a bar of chocolate.
:::

::: {.csf-section}
<h2 class="csf-section__title">What it is — and what it isn't</h2>

::: {.csf-grid}
::: {.csf-card}
<span class="csf-card__icon">✅</span>

### It is
A recurring free potluck in Padova, mostly for people who arrived recently for
work or study, hosted in flats and shared common rooms, roughly monthly.
:::

::: {.csf-card}
<span class="csf-card__icon">🚫</span>

### It isn't
A restaurant, a cooking class, a networking event, a dating app, or a business.
Nobody is paid and nobody pays.
:::

::: {.csf-card}
<span class="csf-card__icon">🤝</span>

### What comes out of it
Neighbours. People do end up passing on flat leads, job tips and a good dentist —
but that happens the way it happens between neighbours, not because it's the agenda.
:::
:::
:::

::: {.csf-section}
<h2 class="csf-section__title">Who runs it</h2>

A small rotating group of people who have been coming since the start. Whoever has
space that month hosts; everyone else brings food. There is no committee, and there
is nothing to join beyond turning up.

If you have a flat with a big enough table and you'd like to host one, tell us —
that is how the next few dinners get scheduled.
:::
